_comment: Atlas Growth UK extensions :: RECOVERY pass 1 over excluded_officp.csv — the BARE-TYPE track. The main config's rule-4 allow is a substring test, so it cannot name the bare Google types 'Contractor' and 'Builder' without also admitting 'Roofing contractor', 'Electrical contractor', 'Deck builder', 'Shed builder'. qualify-leads.js's derived field primary_type with op 'in' IS an exact, case-insensitive test, so this pass takes back exactly the rows whose PRIMARY identity is the bare type — the core of the UK extension ICP ('J Smith Building Services', typed Contractor and nothing else) — with NO name requirement. Deterministic, $0, no re-scrape. Run: node skills/google-maps-scrape/qualify-leads.js --in <run>/maps/excluded_officp.csv --config clients/atlas-growth/recover-baretype-extensions-uk-config.json --out <run>/maps/recover-baretype

qualify_rules._r: 0. RECOVERY SCOPE GATE — only rows the main pass dropped at its positive allow (drop_reason not_in_icp). A row removed by a deny (hard_off_icp_type / off_icp_primary / name_deny) or the floor (too_small) is refused before any other rule is read; this pass can never re-litigate a deny. CAVEAT (same as every recovery config in this client): pointed at a file with NO drop_reason column, `in` reads an empty string and every row is refused — that is the safe failure.
qualify_rules.label: not_a_recovery_candidate

qualify_rules._r: 1. The bare generic types, PRIMARY only, exact match. 'contractor' and 'builder' are the two Google types a UK general builder most often carries alone; 'remodeler' is the generic (non-kitchen, non-bathroom) remodel type; 'building firm' is already a main-pass allow substring and is listed here only so a primary 'Building firm' row dropped for some other allow reason cannot slip away. A row primaried 'Roofing contractor' does NOT match ('roofing contractor' != 'contractor') — that row belongs to the generic name recovery, where its name must claim loft/extension work.
qualify_rules.label: not_bare_generic_primary

qualify_rules._r: 2. Same ghost-listing floor as the main pass (rule 0 already blocks too_small rows; belt and braces for the degraded-run case).
qualify_rules.label: too_small
